title: Game Development Tediousness
author: Patient-Sprinkles920
selftext: Do you know that feeling when your development project really feels like work ? I do and to me that means the game I am working on just isn't fun. Agree / disagree ?

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: Never, I am addicted. It's like a drug and that since 5 months

replies.author: spixt
replies.body:
I was about to say just this (literally word for word, except swap out 5 months with 4 months)

tokenmaxxing my own game has been the most energising and fun/rewarding thing i've ever done in my life. If OP is getting bored, the gamedev life is either not for him or he's doing the wrong project. 

From my own experience, there was literally one day, about 2 months back,  when I realised I had no desire to get on the PC and start adding more features to my game. I thought I finally burned out and was ready to go back to normal. But then around 20 minutes later I started to get a fever and I realised I was just getting sick 😆  About 24 hours of bedrest later, I was back to tokenmaxxin'

replies.author: geddy
replies.body:
\>Creating my own game has been the most energising and fun/rewarding thing i've ever done in my life

I hadn't thought of this, but lately I've had so much more drive and purpose, and I wasn't able to explain it. But it's basically all I think about now. I dive head-first into new hobbies but already being a software guy (but not a game developer), this basically lets me have my dream "job" as a hobby, but without the "staying up all night fixing random bugs" that used to burn me out and make me not want to touch a computer outside of work hours.

comments.author: Post-reality
comments.body:
I am working on my game 18 hours per day, while burning $100-$200 for almost two weeks already. Meanwhile, my real (high-paying) "job" is completely stres-free.

I am completely addicted while stresseing myself out with it.

replies.author: pazh1
replies.body: 200 per day, pure vibecode + something complicated?

replies.author: tingly_sack_69
replies.body: How do you even do your job if you are working on a game "18 hrs a day"

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: In between Claude thinking, and thankfully my work is stress free :)

replies.author: Reign2294
replies.body: Dont tell me you're paying for credits. Do you delegate to other models? Use other API subscriptions claude can call on? Have efficiencies to protect your usage?

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: Opus 5.5 is enough for around 5 days before I need to utilize additional credits, but then there are also external tools I use. I have been experimenting a lot, and reiterating/redrawing a lot of the assets and the features. I guess once I settle down, it'll be down to 50$-60$. Honestly, I don't mind paying more for a faster/better model. It's quite a complicated game with a huge scope, so it may take me a year to finish it off, which is why I would like more powerful model.

replies.author: Reign2294
replies.body: I use 2x Max x20 and 1 Codex 500 for game dev plus a Zai GLM workhorse for cheap work. Never use a single credit. Max usage every week. Sessions run 24 hours a day with input from me via open questions throughout the day.

replies.author: Post-reality
replies.body: I know some let Opus 5.5 assign coding work to other models, but I'm fearful due to how complicated the game is. How does it work for you? Also, could it help Opus 5.5 finish tasks faster? That would be helpful

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body: No, I think the work is something you have to go through. Like training for a large physical challenge or learning a hard skill for a hobby. Sometimes you need to do the hard work to get the reward.

comments.author: gfe_TheHouse
comments.body: If you're not having fun building your game you should consider not doing that. If you're trying to make money doing it, do something else. If you're trying to make games for fun try to make a better game. Not every game is fun.

comments.author: muikrad
comments.body:
As many people said, turns out coding was never the difficult part of making a game 😉

There will be ups and downs.

comments.author: thvaz
comments.body: Testing can get a bit tedious. Marketing is absolutely hell.

comments.author: krazyjakee
comments.body: Get a group of 5 devs and just swap games each week.

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: My ADHD makes anything tedious.  I try to push through it.  But I'm also trying to get medication, because I need to finally finish something.

comments.author: edm-4-life
comments.body: I just spent half a day making wagons, balloons, and pigeons look the way I want. Like, what am I doing?

replies.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
replies.body: That sounds like an interesting game you are working on ?

comments.author: Seven-Prime
comments.body:
Making a game, even with AI, is work. I'm in that stage myself hundreds of assets to build and iterate on.

Keep at it! You got this!

comments.author: geddy
comments.body:
I think you learned something very valuable - if it feels tedious to work on it, the game is likely not very good. At that point, stop working on it. You're describing a solution, not a problem. The problem is that the game is bad, not that working on it is tedious.

I'm a big gamer and have played zero videogames for a month except the one I'm working on currently, and I still can't get enough of it. I keep making it more fun for *me*, because if I'm this into it, people like me who like this particular type of game will most likely enjoy it. Haven't been bored for a single second, I finally can make my dream game and only focus on programming the parts I want to program.

You want tedious? Try fixing weird netcode issues or texturing issues by hand. Or tracking down strange edge-case bugs through all hours of night, like we used to do a year ago and every year before that. That is freakin' tedious. 

In fact... the nerve to claim that asking a robot to build things for you is tedious. Like how fucking lucky are we that we get to be bored because the game WE MADE THE ROBOT DO sucks and isn't "fun" even though WE TOLD THE ROBOT TO MAKE IT!?

Alright, now I'm actually a little pissed off at the audacity of this post.

replies.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
replies.body: Not being spoiled I love the age we live in and how AI has opened enormous possibilities for game creators. I am just saying I was working on this game I thought I would love and I'm just not feeling it. Going back to my turn based strategy game which I love to play and am enhancing it.

comments.author: EconDetective
comments.body: Absolutely not! Vibe coding lets me think of a feature and then implement it with little to no friction. It's so addictive I need to force myself NOT to do it sometimes.

comments.author: SeasawPhilosopher
comments.body: Well not necessarily, sometimes there is just a grind. My game is very fun and in general so is working on it, but man some things are just an absolute grind when you want make to make something coherent and polished. Getting stuff 90% there is amazing fun but that last 10% can be so tedious and boring, like tweaking level layout, fine tuning mechanics, balancing everything. This stuff will probably feel like work for most people and it’s why they’ll fail to take a game from quick AI prototype to something people actually want to play.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body:
Honestly if it feels like work I think you are doing the right thing by handcrafting at least some of it. There should be ups and downs. I get ultra dopamine hits when something tedious I am working on comes together nicely. I get bored working on art or doing something routine that needs to be done but I’ve done many times already. I live for those “I made this and it’s neat!” moments! 

If you aren’t having any of those I would rethink things a little. Make sure your game is somewhat unique. I often think it should say something about you too or at least your particular tastes.

comments.author: Patient-Sprinkles920
comments.body: FYI, I have paused development of the  game that I find tedious and have gone back to expanding on a recent game I love to play. If you love to play them while you develop you can do quick sprints and never have it feel like work ! Thanks to those with supportive comments. To those who thought I am not appreciative of the amazing technology afforded to us that could not be further from the truth. I thought BASIC was manna from heaven when it came out, I am certainly not looking down on AI.
